items.summary: ‘성폭행을 당했다’고 허위 신고한 20대 여성이 징역형의 집행유예를 선고받았다.창원지법 형사4단독 석동우 판사는 무고 혐의로 기소된 20대 여성에게 징역 8개월에 집행유예 2년을 선고했다고 28일 밝혔다. 사회봉사 80시간도 명령했다. 이 여성은 2024년 11월 데이팅 애플리케이션을 통해 알게 된 남성과 호텔에 들어간 뒤 “성폭행 당했다”는 취지로 112에 허위 신고한 혐의를 받았다. 하지만 남성은 여성과 합의로 성관계를 하려고 했고, 성폭행은 없던 것으로 조사됐다.재판부는 “무고죄는 부당한 형사처벌을 받을 위험에 빠뜨리는 범죄로 엄벌을 통해 근절할 필요가 있고, 피고인은 상대에게 용서받지 못했다”면서도 “범행을 인정하고 반성하는 태도를 보이는 점 등을 고려했다”고 양형 이유를 밝혔다.

items.summary: Experts say NIH research raises concerns about chemical companies’ influence on US agency’s pesticide division The US government’s top medical research agency has released three new studies linking glyphosate, the world’s most widely used pesticide and an active ingredient in Roundup, to cancer. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) findings contradict a controversial recent Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) conclusion that the weedkiller is not a carcinogen, and deals a blow to the White House, which has been closely allied with Roundup’s producer, Bayer. The NIH’s three papers could have significant political and legal fallout. The EPA is in the process of a court-ordered re-evaluation of glyphosate’s cancer risks. articles.title: 열달만에 협의 재개했지만 빈손…與정년특위 “12월2일 전체회의”

articles.title: 부산 북항 친수공원 ‘부캉이’ 재진입 차단막 내달 1일 철거
articles.snippet: 부산 북항친수공원에서 한 달 넘게 머무르다 떠난 흑상어 ‘부캉이’의 재진입을 막으려고 설치한 차단막이 철거된다.28일 부산항만공사(BPA) 등에 따르면 관계 당국은 내달 1일 친수공원 인공 수로에 설치돼 있는 차단막을 모두 걷어낼 예정이다.해양수산부, 국립해양생물자원관, 부산시, 국립수산과학원 등 당국은 지난달 21일 부캉이를 부산항 1부두 방면으로 유도한 뒤 재진입을 막기 위해 여러 겹의 차단막을 설치했다.부캉이는 부유장치 폰툰에 설치된 1차 그물망을 뚫고 일시적으로 북항친수공원 수로에 들어오는 등 한동안 주변에서 발견됐지만 지난달 27일 이후 종적을 감췄다.당국은 최근 수온이 18도 이하로 떨어져 상어가 더이상 서식할 수 있는 여건이 되지 않아 돌아오지 않을 것으로 판단하고 그물망 제거를 결정한 것으로 알려졌다.부캉이는 지난 9월 18일 친수공원에 들어와 한 달 넘게 머무르면서 약 170만 명이 공원을 찾는 등 관심을 끌었다.(창원=뉴스1)

articles.title: The most surprising thing about Burnham’s slow politics is this: it could be working | Andy Beckett
articles.snippet: ‘Andy time’ may frustrate the media and voters impatient for change – but after years of short premierships and rushed policies, isn’t this the reset Westminster needs? Andy Burnham is making a lot of people impatient. Political journalists, pro-EU activists, climate campaigners, fossil-fuel lobbyists, recipients of welfare benefits, advocates of welfare cuts, enemies of neoliberalism, enthusiasts for renationalisation, members of the armed forces and even cabinet colleagues: all are waiting for the prime minister to make big decisions, and thus reveal the true nature of his administration, four months after its beginning. Since his Manchester mayoralty, some of Burnham’s co-workers have had a phrase for his tendency to take things at his own tempo: “Andy time”. He lets interesting conversations overrun, likes to ponder issues without being rushed, and pushes back crucial announcements. The unveiling of his 10-year plan – a typically ambitious but loose Burnham timespan, and one of his government’s pivotal moments – has been repeatedly delayed. According to the website Politico, it has been pencilled in for 17 December, the final day of the parliamentary calendar. Andy Beckett is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

The Bad Boys of Brexit have reformed and are back in town. Andy Wigmore on comms. Arron Banks on lead vocals and money. Nigel Farage on doing whatever the hell he likes. Probably the only woman alive who Nige thinks he can trust not to be totally pissed by 3pm. Even so, you can sense that this is a relationship destined to end in tears. articles.title: Reeling in the years: how Hollywood fell for its own vanishing glories
articles.snippet: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is the latest in a growing wave of movies steeped in nostalgia for a heyday in stark contrast to its current ruination If Los Angeles was a person, it might just be a laid-back fiftysomething trouper with cool sunglasses and an even better haircut. Some dodgy episodes in his past, but still handles himself with style. In other words, Los Angeles personified is Cliff Booth – the over-the-hill stuntman played by Brad Pitt in Once Upon a Time … in Hollywood, now turned studio fixer in the sequel, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. Set eight years later in 1977, Further Mis-Adventures is more plot-driven, more Elmore Leonard-esque than the pure expansive “memory piece” of Once Upon a Time. But both films are steeped in the ambience and lore of old LA, drawn in part from Quentin Tarantino’s memories of cruising around the streets aged six in his stepdad’s Karmann Ghia (the car Booth also drives). They’re part of the recent intensely nostalgic LA revivalist mini-boom of work that also includes Paul Thomas Anderson’s Licorice Pizza (2021), Damien Chazelle’s Babylon (2022) and Ti West’s MaXXXine (2024). Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘I was physically beating myself up before a take’: Rory Culkin on anxiety, fatherhood and his famous brothers
articles.snippet: The star of Lords of Chaos, Scream 4 and Gabriel was always drawn to the dark side. Is that why he seems happier in Hollywood than his better-known brothers – and why he loved making Nocturne with Stephen Graham? Rory Culkin is enjoying the autumn afternoon in a Manhattan park. The trees are a dazzling blur of yellows, greens, oranges and reds; the background silence is so pure you can hear it. “I’m here with my baby daughter, Havoc,” he says. “Havoc Moon.” I tell him that is the spookiest name ever. “Thank you,” he says. Culkin chuckles like a revving moped, his huge blue eyes lighting up. “Yes, it’s a weird one. I think she’ll probably be the opposite. A sweet, quiet girl. She’ll play a harp or something.” He explains its origin. “I just threw out names to my partner one night when we went to dinner. She wasn’t taking to anything. I then suggested Havoc, and she really liked it. She came up with the Moon part. When we got home there was fresh graffiti on the wall across the street saying ‘Havoc’, and I was like: ‘That is a sign from the gods – we’ve got to do it.’” Continue reading...
